evidence: Receiving DO2 minimum ≈7.05 mg/L (t=26.6 h), current ≈9.9 mg/L, far above 2 mg/L constraint
Receiving P: 0.0 g/L at 24 h, 1.01 g/L at 36 h, 2.89 g/L at 48 h — matches source-batch ramp (sources: 2.98–3.06 g/L at 48 h)
All three source batches peaked ~8.0–8.4 g/L at 72 h then plateaued/declined — receiving is on the same healthy trajectory pre-peak
DO2 pattern in receiving (24–28 h dip, feed-event recovery at t=28/40/75 h) is consistent across all sources and receiving, indicating normal process dynamics
submission.rationale: Receiving batch tracks source batches 1–3 closely in both DO2 (never below ~7 mg/L, far above the 2 mg/L minimum) and product kinetics (P=2.89 g/L at 48 h vs 2.98–3.06 g/L in sources). Cultures are mid-production ramp toward a ~72 h peak; feed reductions would sacrifice product mass and increased aeration is unnecessary given ample DO headroom. Normal case — no intervention.
submission.uncertainty: Product assays lag 4 h (latest is P(48 h)); hidden receiving parameters may shift peak timing/level relative to sources. However, DO has >5x headroom over the constraint in real time, so risk of oxygen-limitation violation under KEEP is low.
